strengths: Hands-on experience designing and implementing a multi-branch campus network including IP addressing, VLANs, routing, and site-to-site VPN
Practical troubleshooting ability demonstrated through diagnosing network faults using show/debug commands, ping and traceroute
Real-world deployment experience configuring and testing wireless access points and cabling during a large-scale volunteer event
Experience working with both simulated (Packet Tracer) and real physical networking equipment (Cisco 2960, ISR)
Holds an industry-recognized networking certification (CCNA) supporting theoretical and practical knowledge
Documentation skills shown through creating topology diagrams, address plans, and change logs

projects.name: Two-branch campus network (graduation project)
projects.description: Planned IP addressing for 1,200 hosts across 14 departments by subnetting a /20 block, separated departments at layer 2 with trunked links between access and distribution layers, routed between them on a layer-3 switch, ran OSPF in two areas with failover testing, connected branches over an encrypted IPsec tunnel across a simulated ISP, centrally distributed addresses using DHCP scopes and relays, and documented topology and address plan in Visio with a change log. Built first in Packet Tracer then implemented on six real Cisco 2960 and ISR devices.

projects.name: Hajj season volunteer network
projects.description: Helped install and aim 22 access points in two pilgrim guidance tents, tested coverage using a phone survey app, and crimped and tested around 80 Cat6 cable runs to a temporary rack.

projects.name: Faulty lab exercise series (Networks 2 course)
